title: Charge expiry omits the reached end-of-action clear for remaining count 1
behavioral_fact: Charge starts at 2. Normal round-tail processing can reduce it to 1. Reaching the end-of-action cleanup clears exactly count 1 before later Instruct/Dancer processing; count 2 is not cleared by that action cleanup. The clear is not conditional on having used an Electric move or on successfully dealing damage.
prerequisites: Default Charge was successfully used; no special ability/item/state callbacks alter the counter.
Both sides remain able to battle; a later ordinary move attempt reaches its normal end-of-action cleanup.

For the repeat example: a legal positive-PP ordinary Electric move is in the user’s current slots, normal gates pass, and a later ally uses legal Instruct after the user’s ordinary action; no special blacklist, locks, switching, fainting or host fault applies.
minimal_counterexample: Charge succeeds in round n: counter 2, then full round-tail 1. In round n+1 the user performs its normal Electric move: its initial damage reads positive Charge and receives the Charge power multiplier. The normal action end clears counter 1 to 0. A later ally’s Instruct repeats that Electric move in the same round, so the repeat reads 0 and receives no Charge multiplier. A timer-only implementation inferred from WP44 keeps 1 through both actions until the round tail and boosts the repeat incorrectly.
ordinary_control: Immediately after newly setting Charge to 2, reaching that same action’s end leaves it 2; this is distinct from the count-1 clear. Another independent control removes Instruct and still observes the counter clear after the ordinary action.
cancellation_or_partial_commitment: Successful first damage, PP and history stay committed; a later repeat does not undo them. A failed ordinary attempt that reaches the same end cleanup also clears the remaining count. A fault or branch that does not reach the cleanup has no automatic clear guarantee.
needed_consumer: The exact end-of-action count-1 clear is needed in addition to WP43’s positive-count multiplier and WP42’s decrement; current WP40 mentions only an unspecified charge-remnant cleanup.

negative_searches.result: WP44 body fully read; catalog fully read; focused cross-owner search found establishment, positive power multiplier, tail decrement, and WP40’s unspecific cleanup label, but no explicit count-1 clear or repeat regression.

minimal_revision: Add the reached action-end rule: if remaining Charge is exactly 1, clear it before later repeated-move consumers. Keep the existing 2 establishment, tail decrement, failure-stage and execution caveats. Name the exact rule at WP40’s cleanup handoff.
preserved_scope: No new Charge duration or persistent field design.
No change to the default positive Charge multiplier or round-tail decrement.
No claim about runtime media, host recovery, or every exceptional callback.
acceptance_regression: Establish 2, same-action cleanup preserves 2.
Full round tail reduces 2 to 1.
Reached ordinary action cleanup changes 1 to 0 regardless of move type or damage success.
A successful Electric move then same-round legal Instruct has Charge multiplier only on the first use.
An earlier fault that does not reach action cleanup is a separately conditional case.
dependencies: WP40 reached action cleanup and repeat execution
rebuttal_target: Show an existing frozen formal clause that already defines exactly 1→0 before repeated-move consumers, or show the legal repeat cannot occur under the listed conditions.

title: Fang status immunity short-circuits the status random draw before the flinch draw
behavioral_fact: Once a Fang secondary callback is actually reached and its internal chance is positive, it queries status eligibility first. Only an eligible status consumes its own status draw. The subsequent flinch draw is separate and still occurs when status is ineligible; it occurs before the Inner Focus rejection at flinch submission. The outer secondary-effect gate is a separate earlier draw; the default Thunder Fang outer chance is 101.
prerequisites: Default Thunder Fang with ordinary command/PP/target checks passing.
The damage route reaches the secondary callback: calculated damage positive, no Sheer Force suppression, no active Shield Dust unless ignored, no substitute absorption.
Current mechanics use Electric-type paralysis immunity; actual target is pure Electric, remains alive, has no Inner Focus and no callback altering the status eligibility or counter.
No additional chance modifiers: internal chance 10. All earlier accuracy/critical/variance/outer draws fixed separately; the next two available internal random values are 5, then 99.
minimal_counterexample: Against an Electric target, paralysis eligibility is false before any status random draw. The first available internal random value 5 is consumed by flinch, so Flinch becomes true; 99 is not consumed inside that Fang callback. Reading “separately draw for status and flinch” as an unconditional pair instead consumes 5 on an impossible paralysis and 99 on flinch, producing false and shifting later random consumers.
ordinary_control: With an otherwise identical target that is not paralysis-immune, internal 5 produces paralysis, then internal 99 does not flinch. If status submission immediately cures the new status, that submission and its cure callbacks still happened before the flinch draw. Another independent control has active Inner Focus: the flinch draw is still consumed, but its commit is rejected.
cancellation_or_partial_commitment: The hit’s damage/PP/history are already committed before the internal callback. Immunity cancels only the status branch’s draw/commit, not the subsequent flinch draw. Status application and immediate cure are not rolled back by a later failed flinch commit.
needed_consumer: Conditional random-consumption order needs the actual status query before the draw and the flinch commit after its own draw; two independent marginal chances alone do not define the sequence.

negative_searches.result: Full assigned formal text has two separate draws and component immunity, but does not specify the status-eligibility short circuit or a Fang internal random-consumption vector.

minimal_revision: Qualify the Fang rule: query the chosen status first and draw its internal roll only if eligible; then independently draw for flinch and apply flinch’s own commit guard. Keep the distinct outer secondary gate and chance modifiers.
preserved_scope: No claim that all secondary effects share Fang’s draw order.
No change to the 10% internal base chances or ordinary chance modifiers.
No runtime or global replay claim.
acceptance_regression: Reached callback with status eligible: next internal 5,99 applies status, no flinch; two draws.
Reached callback with status immune: next internal 5,99 flinches; one internal draw, 99 remains for later consumer.
Positive chance and Inner Focus: draw consumed but flinch not committed.
Substitute, zero internal chance, or outer suppression skips the respective callback/draw path.
dependencies: WP43 probability helper and outer gate
WP44 status eligibility and flinch commit
rebuttal_target: Demonstrate that the frozen formal wording already fixes conditional draw consumption, or that the listed default Thunder Fang callback cannot be reached.

title: Psycho Shift uses generic status eligibility and bypasses sleep/freeze clause wrappers
behavioral_fact: Psycho Shift target eligibility calls the generic status query directly. The rule module adds Sleep Clause/Modified Sleep Clause and Freeze Clause only to the dedicated sleep/freeze queries, not to that generic query. Sleep Talk can legally choose Psycho Shift and calls it through the special route, allowing an actually sleeping user to reach the transfer.
prerequisites: Sleep Clause or Modified Sleep Clause is enabled and no later plugin replaces these queries.
User is sleeping with remaining count 2 before its ordinary Sleep Talk check; Sleep Talk reduces it to 1 but remains usable while asleep.
User knows legal Sleep Talk plus Psycho Shift; Psycho Shift is the only eligible called candidate, no contrary slot restrictions, no no-PP Sleep Talk failure.

Opposing target is alive, raw status NONE, with a different opposing non-egg party member already sleeping. Generic status guards pass: no substitute/protection, terrain/Uproar/status immunity, Prankster Dark restriction, reflection or callback affecting this example.
The target submission’s random sleep duration and any later cures are fixed separately; no held cure/ability cure exists in the minimal vector.
minimal_counterexample: The already sleeping opposing party member makes an ordinary direct sleep effect fail the dedicated Sleep Clause query. Under the same opposing party state, Sleep Talk calls Psycho Shift: generic status eligibility accepts the empty-status target, the target receives a newly chosen sleep duration, and the user is then cured. The same wrapper bypass exists structurally for transferring frozen status, without claiming a default ordinary frozen-user route.
ordinary_control: Keep the target’s generic guards and party state identical, but use ordinary SleepTarget through its dedicated sleep query: the clause rejects it and no target sleep is committed. Independently clear the existing opposing sleep: dedicated sleep and the generic transfer can both pass their respective queries.
cancellation_or_partial_commitment: Sleep Talk’s own PP and its initial sleep decrement are prior commitments. Called Psycho Shift uses special usage and does not consume a persistent Psycho Shift slot’s PP through the simple new-move route. Target status submission and its reactions precede the user cure; later cure/failure does not imply no target submission occurred.
needed_consumer: The clause-wrapper consumer boundary must be distinguished from the generic eligibility used by Psycho Shift; declaring only “target must accept status” leaves the exception unresolved.

negative_searches.result: WP44 body/effect coverage and full shared catalog freshly read; focused formal search found generic Psycho Shift acceptance plus ordinary clause descriptions, but no explicit Psycho Shift generic-query exception or regression.
Fresh exact-range inspection found wrappers for dedicated sleep, Yawn, freeze; no generic-query clause wrapper in the inspected rule block.

minimal_revision: State in Psycho Shift’s bounded rule that it uses generic status eligibility and does not inherit the dedicated sleep/freeze clause wrapper. Add the ordinary direct sleep versus Sleep Talk→Psycho Shift control, leaving generic immunity/terrain/protection unchanged.
preserved_scope: Retain specialized clause behavior on ordinary dedicated sleep/freeze and Yawn.
Do not assert all forced calls or debug submissions bypass all guards.
Do not invent a default frozen-user route.
acceptance_regression: Enabled Sleep Clause, opposing reserve asleep, empty target: ordinary direct sleep rejected.
Same state, eligible Sleep Talk calls Psycho Shift: user sleep 2→1, target new sleep, user cured; outer PP remains spent.
Added generic terrain or immunity gate rejects transfer while keeping earlier Sleep Talk/PP commitments.
Target immediate cure case still registers the prior submission and subsequent user cure.
dependencies: WP44 generic status query and clause entry boundaries
WP47-A Sleep Talk pool and special call
WP40 special usage skip and PP/history
WP46/50 immediate cures and stage commitment
rebuttal_target: Show an existing frozen formal exception for Psycho Shift’s clause-wrapper bypass or prove the listed ordinary Sleep Talk pool rejects Psycho Shift.

title: Late Protean/Libero Curse target reconstruction does not run a second redirection pass
proposed_severity: MEDIUM if classified as a missing behavioral boundary; otherwise retain as an observation
claim: The late Curse target reconstruction after Protean/Libero is observably different from the initial Ghost Curse construction/redirection path. WP47-A §5.1 and WP47-B §3.1 currently describe the initial dynamic target/redirection behavior; WP40 step14 and WP49 Protean row acknowledge reselecting a foe but do not explicitly say that the late list is not passed through redirection again. This is proposed as a bounded clarification/coverage finding, not a self-adjudicated contradiction.
prerequisites: Generation8 ordinary double battle; all four seats alive and near. User at seat0 starts with current WATER type, active PROTEAN, valid ordinary CURSE slot, HP101/101 and positive PP. A CURSE-capable GENGAR can have this current type via SOAK and PROTEAN via allowed Skill Swap; this review assumes the already-established legal state and does not claim execution of that acquisition chain.

User Attack/Defense/Speed stages are zero and their changes permitted, so the initial non-Ghost Curse whole-use gate passes. User and targets retain their types/state during this use except the intended Protean change.

Foes at seats1 and3 are uncursed, with seat1 Follow Me marker1 established by a valid earlier action and seat3 unmarked. Fixed random foe selection chooses seat3. No Spotlight/other redirection, Stalwart/Propeller Tail, semi-invulnerability, Magic Coat/Bounce, move blocking, Substitute/protection, type-data gaps, healing item, ability suppression or other callback state changes. Normal feedback/animation return.
minimal_counterexample: Initial current user type is WATER, so initial target category remains User and the list is empty. Initial redirection returns at its single-foe/list-size guard.

After ordinary PP/history and initial whole-use admission, Protean changes current type to GHOST. The specific late Curse branch clears preselection and reconstructs a RandomNearFoe list, with fixed result seat3.

This branch calls the target-construction operation only. The next phase performs empty-list/initial success checks; it does not revisit redirection. Seat3 receives Curse and user HP becomes51, while seat1 remains uncursed despite Follow Me.
Applying the §5.1 normal construction-plus-redirection chain a second time would instead select seat1; that behavior is not the fixed-reference late branch.
ordinary_control: Change only the starting user current type to GHOST: initial target construction already uses RandomNearFoe, fixed choice seat3 is redirected by Follow Me to seat1, Protean does not alter the type, seat1 is cursed and user HP becomes51.

Remove only active Protean from the WATER-start fixture: initial target remains User/empty and the non-Ghost general effect requests Speed−1 then Attack+1 then Defense+1; no Curse HP cost and neither foe is cursed.
partial_commits_under_cancellation: At initial whole-use failure because all three non-Ghost stage requests are unavailable, ordinary PP/history are already committed, while the later Protean change/reconstruction/Curse/HP cost have not occurred.

Once the late Protean change has happened, it is not locally rolled back if the rebuilt target is already cursed or if an unrelated later callback fails; ordinary PP/history and any reached type write remain.

For a successful Curse target main effect, the target mark precedes user HP expenditure and HP-item check. An exception/cancellation after a reached write does not justify undoing that prefix. This proposal does not specify host recovery, continued process execution or diagnostic retries.

negative_search.query: 诅咒|CURSE|CurseTarget|PROTEAN|LIBERO|变幻自在|自由者 across the formal combat-requirements directory; matching relevant context read as above
negative_search.result: WP40/WP49 do state late reselecting a foe. No second-redirection exclusion was found in the fully read WP47 bodies/test catalog or in these bounded related rows. This does not assert a full read or universal negative over all other formal files.

minimal_revision: Add one exception sentence to WP47-A §5.1 and a cross-reference on the Curse row in WP47-B: when the initial User target list is empty and Protean/Libero later makes the user Ghost, the special reconstruction chooses a foe but does not run the redirection layer a second time. Add a static paired regression without changing existing MA-T07–T10, which explicitly keep type stable.
retained_scope: Initial-Ghost Curse redirection, non-Ghost stat changes, existing dynamic-target tests, source behavior and no-runtime scope remain intact.
No new implementation, architecture, source fix or official-game correction is proposed.
acceptance_regression: The WATER/active-Protean fixture must statically predict final seat3, seat3 Curse true, seat1 false and user HP51.
The only-starting-type-Ghost control must predict seat1, seat1 Curse true, seat3 false and user HP51.
The no-Protean WATER control must predict empty list and own stage changes with no Curse HP payment.
All scenarios remain NOT_EXECUTED until a separately authorized reference-host run; no static table result can be marked a runtime PASS.

evidence_level: STATIC_SOURCE_READ + STATIC_CONTROL_FLOW_DERIVATION; not isolated-reference, independent-model or full-host/Demo execution

title: 合法可查询效果名命中不能构造的既有绑定时，不经过无实现回退
proposed_severity: MEDIUM if valid-data premise and missing-boundary interpretation survive counter-review; otherwise observation
prerequisites: Human-authored registered move identity, valid ordinary type/target/category/power/PP data, legal query-name string, no additional binding/plugin or later source override.
Use exact effect identity CRITICAL_HIT_RATIOS. The existing named value belongs to the fixed reference and is an array instance, not a constructible move implementation.
This is a conditional author-data boundary, not a default740 binding defect. Default401 effect bindings all locate definitions.
behavioral_fact: The factory tests whether a named binding exists, then asks that actual resolved receiver to construct a move. It does not first verify receiver construction capability. The existing critical-rate value satisfies name existence but is an array instance; the construction request fails before the fallback branch. This differs from an absent legally queryable name.
minimal_counterexample: Registered Physical/Power40 data with code CRITICAL_HIT_RATIOS resolves the existing array value, then fails the constructor request (NoMethodError class under ordinary Ruby receiver semantics). Status/Power0 fails at the same construction boundary; neither reaches whole-use fallback failure/damage. The claim remains pending independent validation of the exact valid-data premise and whether WP43 absence wording already excludes this named-but-nonconstructible case.
ordinary_control: Only change code to absent ReviewMissingEffect: factory chooses Unimplemented; valid status then fails at whole-use gate, valid Physical40 continues common damage. Code None independently constructs the known ordinary no-extra-effect behavior.
failure_cancel_partial_commit: Factory failure occurs before the constructed move can be used. Direct conversion has no move-use PP/damage commit. A simple called entrance attempts construction before its own pbUseMove call; outer caller PP/history/random choices may already be committed, but they require their own concrete caller fixture and are not automatically rolled back. No host crash/retry/recovery result is claimed.

counter_scope_analysis.absence_interpretation: WP43 line31 is conditioned on not finding the effect implementation, and line35 plus catalog235 explicitly use the absent ReviewMissingEffect identity. A narrow reference-lookup reading treats an existing named value as outside that absence premise. The vectors therefore remain correct under that reading.
counter_scope_analysis.possible_clarification: The body does not explicitly define whether “implementation not found” means no named binding versus no constructible behavior. An independent implementation reader could regard a resolved nonconstructible value as “no effect implementation” and expect fallback. Clarifying the distinction would avoid this ambiguity while preserving architecture neutrality.
counter_scope_analysis.recommendation: Retain the source behavior as a conditional author-data boundary observation, or accept a small compatibility clarification if root considers line31 to quantify over all valid registered codes without constructible behavior. Do not label it default corruption, a demonstrated runtime crash, or a broken R5 absent-name regression. This counter-review recommends observation/clarification rather than automatic MEDIUM promotion.
